```yaml
name: CI/CD

on:
  push:
    branches: [ main ]
  pull_request:
    branches: [ main ]

jobs:
  ci:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - name: Checkout code
        uses: actions/checkout@v2

      - name: Set up Elixir
        uses: erlef/setup-elixir@v1
        with:
          elixir-version: '1.13'
          otp-version: '24'

      - name: Install dependencies
        run: mix deps.get --only dev test

      - name: Run tests
        run: mix test

      - name: Run linting
        run: mix format --check-formatted

      - name: Run quality check
        run: mix quality

  release:
    needs: ci
    if: github.ref == 'refs/heads/main' && github.event_name == 'push'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - name: Checkout code
        uses: actions/checkout@v2

      - name: Set up Elixir
        uses: erlef/setup-elixir@v1
        with:
          elixir-version: '1.13'
          otp-version: '24'

      - name: Install dependencies
        run: mix deps.get --only prod

      - name: Build release
        run: MIX_ENV=prod mix release

      - name: Create release tag
        run: |
          git config user.name "GitHub Actions"
          git config user.email "actions@github.com"
          git tag v$(git describe --tags --abbrev=0) -a -m "Release v$(git describe --tags --abbrev=0)"
          git push origin v$(git describe --tags --abbrev=0)

      - name: Trigger release workflow
        id: trigger_release
        uses: pascalgn/retry-action@v2
        with:
          max_attempts: 5
          delay_minutes: 1
          action: ./.github/workflows/release.yml
          inputs: '{"ref": "refs/tags/v$(git describe --tags --abbrev=0)"}'
```

This GitHub Actions workflow file sets up both a CI and a release pipeline for your Elixir project. The CI pipeline runs on every push or pull request to the `main` branch, ensuring that your code is tested, linted, and passes a quality check before any changes can be merged. The release pipeline is triggered manually when a new tag is pushed to the repository, building a release and creating a new tag for it.
